assessment.nobel_worthiness: The KPZ equation is the canonical minimal model of non-equilibrium interface growth: a single nonlinear stochastic equation that defines a universality class with exact exponents and Tracy-Widom statistics in one dimension. It links growth, directed polymers, random matrices and integrable probability, which is exactly the kind of simple, general mechanism that organises many messy systems. Its impact on non-equilibrium statistical physics is deep and lasting.
assessment.attribution: The 1986 KPZ paper was by Kardar, Parisi and Zhang. Parisi already holds a 2021 prize, so a fair configuration would credit Kardar and Zhang, with Takeuchi's experimental confirmation as an optional third name. I am uncertain whether the committee would rather include the experimental confirmation than recognise the theory alone. Other theorists who solved the 1D case exactly are not in the credited names and cannot be added.
assessment.maturity: Mature for the theory (about 40 years of work and exact solutions). Experimental confirmation in liquid-crystal turbulence (Takeuchi and Sano, 2010 onward) is clear and independently reproduced in several systems, though some experiments show only partial agreement with the predicted statistics. Recognition is timely.
uncertainties: Whether the Parisi 2021 prize makes the committee reluctant to honour a paper he co-authored.
Whether the experimental confirmation is considered decisive enough to merit a laureate slot for Takeuchi.
I have not independently verified the details of the experimental scope or its limits.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: The quantum spin Hall effect and the Z2 topological insulator opened a whole field of topological band theory. They established that bulk invariants guarantee protected boundary states, and the idea spread to photonics, cold atoms and phononics. The concept is clean, general and experimentally rich.
assessment.attribution: Kane and Mele made the theoretical prediction and introduced the Z2 invariant (2005). Molenkamp's group gave the first experimental realisation in HgTe quantum wells (2007), following the Bernevig-Hughes-Zhang proposal. BHZ, Fu-Kane-Mele three-dimensional work and Hasan's ARPES experiments are not in the credited names, so the three-person split is defensible but contested.
assessment.maturity: Highly mature: many independent confirmations in HgTe, Bi-based 3D materials and elsewhere over nearly two decades. The 2016 prize covered topological phase transitions in a different setting, so the committee must judge how much overlap that leaves.
uncertainties: Overlap with the 2016 prize and the contested role of the BHZ and Fu-Kane-Mele works.
Unresolved priority questions for the 3D topological insulator discovery, which cannot be settled with the supplied names alone.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: The jamming picture explains how disordered packings of grains, foams and emulsions become rigid. It supplies a critical point with scaling and a universal mechanism (isostaticity, excess low-frequency modes) for glassy and granular matter. It is simple, analysable and connects well to experiment, and the concept has been valuable across soft matter.
assessment.attribution: The 1998 Liu-Nagel jamming phase diagram and the O'Hern-Silbert-Liu-Nagel work on point J are the central contributions. A two-person credit is natural. Other contributors, such as those on isostaticity and the mean-field theory of jamming, are not in the credited names and cannot be added.
assessment.maturity: Moderately mature. Numerics and experiments agree on many scaling exponents, but whether jamming is a true critical phenomenon with the same universality in all dimensions, and how it relates to the glass transition, is still debated. Recognition is plausible but not overdue.
uncertainties: Whether the jamming point is truly a critical phase transition remains open.
The link to the glass transition is incomplete, which might make the prize look premature.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: The 1984 BPZ work on infinite conformal symmetry in two-dimensional quantum field theory gave exact solutions for critical phenomena, classifications of universality classes and the foundations of string-worldsheet theory. It is a very clear case of a foundational paper that contained almost everything, with enormous lasting influence in statistical mechanics.
assessment.attribution: The standard credit is Belavin, Polyakov and Zamolodchikov, which matches the supplied names. Polyakov was the main driver of the bootstrap concept. The role of Friedan, Qiu and Shenker, and of Cardy in applications, is not in the supplied credit and is a possible allocation question.
assessment.maturity: The theory is thoroughly confirmed through exact critical exponents, minimal models and Ising and Potts experiments, and it has been mature for decades. Recognition is arguably overdue. The mathematical-physics character may not suit a prize that favours discoveries about nature.
uncertainties: Whether the committee sees this as a physical discovery or as mathematical structure.
Missing credit for Cardy, Friedan, Qiu and Shenker would be a point of dispute.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: The flat bands at the magic angle in twisted bilayer graphene, with correlated insulators and superconductivity, opened the field of moire quantum materials. The Bistritzer-MacDonald continuum model is a clean, analytical route to the magic angle, and the experiments revealed a tunable strongly correlated platform. It is a major, creative result.
assessment.attribution: Bistritzer and MacDonald made the 2011 theoretical prediction. Jarillo-Herrero's group (with Cao et al., 2018) observed the correlated insulator and superconductivity. Dean, Kim, Yazdani and others contributed key experiments, so the three-way split carries real dispute about the experimental side.
assessment.maturity: Still young. The pairing mechanism, the interplay of topology and interactions, and the reproducibility across devices are not yet settled. Recognition may be early, though the pace of progress and the independent confirmations are strong.
uncertainties: Experimental credit beyond Jarillo-Herrero is disputed.
Premature compared with other mature condensed-matter candidates.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Ultracold atoms in optical lattices realise Hubbard-type models with tunable parameters, including the superfluid to Mott-insulator transition, and enable quantum simulation of many-body physics. This makes theoretical models directly testable in controlled experiments, which I value. Impact on quantum many-body physics is lasting.
assessment.attribution: Zoller and Jaksch proposed the Hubbard-model implementation (1998), Greiner and Bloch observed the Mott transition (2002), and Esslinger's fermionic work is also decisive. The list has four names while a prize can carry only three, so a choice is forced and the pick of Greiner over Esslinger is uncertain. Ketterle, Cornell and Wieman were already honoured in 2001 for BEC.
assessment.maturity: Mature in its core results, with many independent labs. Quantum simulation of open problems such as high-Tc physics is still developing. Recognition is timely.
uncertainties: The choice among Greiner, Esslinger and Bloch for the experimental slot is contested.
Possible overlap with a quantum-computing prize involving Zoller.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Optical lattice clocks reached fractional uncertainty of about 1e-18, enabling tests of fundamental physics and relativistic geodesy. The magic-wavelength proposal is simple and elegant, and the instrument is a major advance in precision measurement.
assessment.attribution: Katori proposed the magic-wavelength lattice clock (2001-03), and Ye's group delivered record accuracy and many-body clocks. A two-person credit fits the supplied names. Hall and Hansch were honoured for frequency combs in 2005, and others who contributed (for example Lemonde, Derevianko) are not included.
assessment.maturity: Mature and widely confirmed across many labs, with a redefinition of the second under discussion. Recognition appears timely.
uncertainties: Whether the prize would be seen as technology and metrology rather than a physics discovery.
Credit for the ion-clock community, for example Wineland, who has a prize already.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Wavefront shaping and time reversal show that multiple scattering, long seen as pure disorder, can be controlled and inverted. The transmission-eigenchannel picture connects directly to random-matrix theory (bimodal transmission distributions, DMPK), which I find compelling. It has led to imaging through scattering media and applications in acoustics, optics and medicine.
assessment.attribution: Vellekoop and Mosk demonstrated optical wavefront shaping (2007). Fink pioneered time-reversal mirrors and acoustic focusing. The scattering-matrix and eigenchannel theory also owes much to Dorokhov, Mello and Beenakker, who are not in the supplied credit. The three names support a fair configuration, but the unity of the discovery is unclear.
assessment.maturity: Experimentally well confirmed in optics and acoustics, though the conceptual novelty compared with phase conjugation and earlier ideas is argued, and it may be seen as more of a method than a discovery.
uncertainties: The compound character of the discovery may need separate recognition for acoustic and optical parts.
Missing theory credit for transmission eigenchannels.
Whether the committee will see enough novelty in the physics.
